payload.title: feedback_store._evidence_refs_from_item still reads what a sample item cites in its own way (dict paths without lines, string evidence ignored) beside the new owner item_citations.item_cited_refs, and the item_citations atlas family does not name it, so the operator batch label's evidence_refs disagree with the refs the judges were handed.
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback_store.py:2143-2150 (reads item path and dict evidence paths only: no line, string refs dropped)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback_store.py:1138 (its one caller: the evidence_refs of an operator batch label whose verdict names none)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/item_citations.py:53-64 (the owner: item_cited_refs returns path:line refs and string refs, in order)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/ownership_atlas.py:112-114 (the item_citations family forbids other names but not _evidence_refs_from_item)
aria-kernel/tests/test_item_citations.py:8-11 (the owner's own test names this reader among the four that disagreed)
payload.rule_violated: PLAN-v2 section 1.2 one owner per fact; the item_citations family exists so a fifth reader of an item's citations cannot drift from the owner (the same defect as the retired system_one_points._cited_line).
payload.notes: For an item {path P, evidence ["P:120", {path Q, line 7}]} the owner returns [P, P:120, Q:7] while _evidence_refs_from_item returns [P, Q]: the string ref is dropped and no line survives. An operator label recorded through record_batch with no explicit evidence_refs therefore carries refs that name no line and miss a ref the judges cited, and the atlas invariant stays green because the family lists names, not this one. Close condition: Make _evidence_refs_from_item a caller of item_citations.item_cited_refs (or delete it and call the owner at feedback_store.py:1138), add the name to the item_citations family's forbidden names, and pin that a label for an item with dict evidence carries [P, P:120]. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
